title: The Overpaid Fare and the Long Drive Back
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] I have been driving a taxi for eleven years now, and most nights blend together into one long, tired blur.
Narrator: [reflective] But one night last spring still stands out clearly, because of something small that happened right at the very end of a ride.
Narrator: [honestly] A young tourist got into my car late at night, exhausted after a long flight, and asked me to take him to his hotel.
Narrator: [gently] He didn't speak our language well, and he seemed nervous about handling unfamiliar money, so he simply handed me a folded bundle of cash.
Narrator: [thoughtful] He said, please just take what I owe you, since I don't fully understand the currency yet after arriving today.
Narrator: [with feeling] I counted it later under a streetlight and realized he had accidentally given me almost four times the actual fare.
Narrator: [reflective] It was already close to midnight, my shift had technically ended, and I was genuinely exhausted after a long, difficult day of driving.
Narrator: [determined] Still, I turned my taxi around and drove back toward his hotel, because keeping that money felt like stealing from someone who trusted me completely.
Narrator: [honestly] When I found him in the lobby, he looked confused, and then embarrassed, once I explained his simple counting mistake.
Narrator: [warmly] He tried to insist I keep the extra money anyway, calling it a generous tip for driving all the way back so late.
Narrator: [sincere] I told him gently that returning it wasn't generosity on my part, it was simply what honesty required of me that night.
Narrator: [peacefully] He shook my hand for a long moment before finally going upstairs, and I drove home feeling something warmer than any large tip could have given me.
Narrator: [warmly] My family still doesn't fully understand why I turned down that extra money during such a tiring week, but I've never once regretted the decision.
